generatedProse.concept-context: In psychology, progressing works the same way across a module. A confusing result in a statistics task, or a low mark on a lab report, becomes information about what to work on next. That feeds the self-belief to keep going and a mastery goal, such as getting better at interpreting data, that outlasts any one assignment.
generatedProse.worked-example: Two psychology students struggle with the research-methods module. One reads a poor mark on an early practical as proof they are not a numbers person, and aims only to scrape a pass. The other treats it as information, builds confidence by working through one statistical test at a time, and sets a goal to understand how to analyse data, not just pass the exam. By the end of the module, the second student handles methods with real ease.
generatedProse.summary: In psychology, the three habits work best as one practice you repeat across a module. You read a hard result as information, build the self-belief and learning motivation to keep going, and set a mastery goal that builds real understanding. Running that round after round is what moves your psychology study forward.

check.body: A student gets a poor mark on an early essay. They read the feedback as showing what to work on, build their confidence by improving one weak area at a time, and set a goal to get better at structuring an argument. By the end of term their essays are stronger. What does this show?

items.text: Their next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following report improved.
Nothing; feedback comes at the end, so it cannot affect anything that follows.
Only the mark on the first report, which cannot now change.
The deadline for the next report.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using the feedback fed back into the next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following report improved: that is the cycle working.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student changed before the next report, not the old mark or the deadline.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Using the feedback fed back into the student's next round of learning and preparation, which is why the next report improved. The old mark cannot change and the deadline is not part of the cycle; feedback is not the end, it feeds the next turn.

_items.text: That the three habits worked as one practice: a growth response, self-belief and learning motivation, and a mastery goal, each feeding the next across the term.
_items.feedback: Yes. All three ran together, round after round, and the work improved.

_items.text: That the first poor mark was a fair verdict on their ability.
_items.feedback: The point is the opposite: the student treated the mark as information, not a verdict.

_items.text: That only the final essay mark matters, not what came before it.
_items.feedback: What came before is the point. The habits across the term made the later work stronger.

_items.text: That setting a goal alone was enough, with no change in mindset or effort.
_items.feedback: The goal worked because a growth response and real effort sat behind it.
